title: The Orchard That Walks Itself

features.name: rotating rows
features.desc-on-touch: the orchard turns slowly as you watch, each row holding a different compass bearing than the last. the trees remember being planted elsewhere, and they're teaching the ground to shift around them.

features.name: dropped maps
features.desc-on-touch: three folded paper surveys lie against the base of the nearest trunk. each one plots the orchard in a different shape, different scale. the most recent is still warm.

features.name: dust motes in angled light
features.desc-on-touch: golden dust hangs in the gap between row-shadows. light arrives from two suns simultaneously and refuses to pick a direction.

features.name: the furthest tree
features.desc-on-touch: one eucalyptus stands deeper in the orchard than the rows should allow. it's not moving. something that walks always knows where home is.

features.name: soil taste
features.desc-on-touch: the earth under your feet carries flavours of seven different properties, seven different years of rain. the orchard is remembering where it came from one mouthful at a time.

inscription: each row learns to walk in its own direction; the orchard moves like a school of things that only look like trees
